clue.text: Possibly paint again in about a month or at the end of June

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
Dec is the abbreviation for December

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, taken here from June

explanation.surface: Someone plans to repaint a room, sometime within a month or by late June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as one example: you might repaper rather than paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Repainting a room is one way of doing up its decor afresh, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Short road to defeat

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a road is a route

explanation.surface: A quick way to beat someone is a short cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat, and to rout is to defeat utterly.

clue.text: Rick is upset with cold tea

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rick is annoyed his tea has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a name; it is a verb meaning to wrench a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To rick a joint is to sprain or wrench it, close in sense to putting it out of place.

clue.text: Chief exec has to swing wavering father in rethink

indicators.note: has means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CEO is chief executive officer
to swing from a rope is to hang

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so the letters of father are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boss has to persuade a hesitant father to reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' puts HANG inside CEO; 'wavering' turns FATHER into FHEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a reversal of one's opinion or plan after thinking again.

clue.text: Salt level

definitions.meaning: an old salt is a sailor; a naval sailor below officer rank has this name
a grade or standing on a scale

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a non-commissioned sailor and a classification or grade.

clue.text: Trinidad's first 15? Wrong! Right!

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word Trinidad

parts.note: 15-across means pitiless; wrong it, giving its opposite, and you get ruthful, full of pity

explanation.surface: A cricket-style cry: Trinidad's opening fifteen got it wrong, then right.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to 15-across; its opposite is the old word RUTHFUL, compassionate.
explanation.definitionFit: A truthful statement is correct, so the exclamation agrees with it.

clue.text: Rip off bits of clothing aggressively during kinky sex

indicators.note: during puts the picked letters in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: S and M, sadomasochism, is the kinky sex

indicators.note: bits of the two following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A lurid picture of clothes being torn off in a frenzy of rough sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip someone off is to swindle them, and a swindle is a con trick.

clue.text: Wine company carries conviction

indicators.note: carries means holds, so the wine goes inside the company

parts.note: red is red wine

explanation.surface: A wine firm is found guilty in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests a court verdict; here it is a firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, and a conviction is a firmly held belief.

clue.text: New revolutionary leader surrounds city

indicators.note: surrounds means goes around, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: a master is a leader or chief
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A newly risen revolutionary chief takes control of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a major city in north-west England, so the definition names its kind.

clue.text: Brash newcomer put off entertaining celebrity

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece goes inside the other
off means wrong or awry, so the letters of put are jumbled

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A cocky arrival is offended at hosting a famous name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like one verb meaning deterred; 'off' alone scrambles PUT into UPT, which holds STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves with presumptuous arrogance.

clue.text: Infected relative with a touch of norovirus

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: a touch of a word is just a trace of it, its first letter

explanation.surface: A family member has caught a mild dose of the winter vomiting bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infected is contaminated or impure, which is what unclean means.

clue.text: Do you start to toss them in sweet sauce?

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the sauce

parts.note: custard is a sweet sauce poured over puddings
you is often written U in text-speak

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter, here of toss

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether you begin by tossing something in custard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like an auxiliary verb opening the question; it is the definition, meaning to suffice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be good enough, and 'that will do' expresses the same sufficiency.

clue.text: Supply nothing to hotel over the hill?

indicators.note: read as the adverb from supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel is starved of supplies, as if in a bad review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb meaning provide; it is the adverb of supple, the anagram signal for the fourteen letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for being old, past one's prime; the question mark flags the hill as figurative.

clue.text: Irrigate large area, harvesting a small salad plant

parts.note: to irrigate is to water

indicators.note: harvesting means removing a crop, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: acres form a large area of land

explanation.surface: Watering a big field while gathering a little salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercress is a peppery leaf eaten in salads, so it is one example of a salad plant.

clue.text: Flower seller on the Internet

definitions.meaning: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the great South American one
the online retail giant of that name

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the South American river and to the online shopping company.

clue.text: The slurs about being callous

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Insults that are hurled about are cruel and unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone without pity or compassion: synonyms.

clue.text: Issue about sport being widely read

indicators.note: about means around, so the issue goes round the sport

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is an edition
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A sports magazine number that sells to a large readership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widely read' suggests a popular magazine; it means a person who has read a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning, the state of having studied many books.

clue.text: Mix ink and water in Jersey etc …

indicators.note: mix means stir together, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Blending ink with water on a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the island; it is the woolly garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, one example of knitted garments in general.

clue.text: I'll never forget retired footballer and knight wearing cap

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or going back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Pelé, the Brazilian footballer

indicators.note: wearing puts the knight inside the cap, which he has on

parts.note: a cap is a hat
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A famous player, now retired, and a knight in his cap stride out together.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the animal speaking: the saying is that an elephant never forgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially this animal has a perfect memory, so the definition is what it would say of itself.

clue.text: Setter's stuck with English attribute

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'm, I am
stuck means placed or put

explanation.surface: The compiler grumbles about being saddled with a dull English quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute a fault to someone is to attribute or ascribe it to them: synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: … seen here in president's resumé

indicators.note: in means the islands go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Pres is the abbreviation for president
the ellipsis carries over Jersey etc from the previous clue: the Channel Islands, CI

explanation.surface: Something from the previous clue appears in a president's CV.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 17-down: 'Jersey etc' there are the Channel Islands, CI.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis and a résumé are both a concise summary of a longer text: synonyms.

clue.text: Typical daily routine before TV show is a nervous habit

indicators.note: before places the routine ahead of the TV show

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char
a comedian's routine is an act
ER is the American hospital drama series
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone's habitual pre-television ritual is a sign of their anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily (short for daily woman) or char is a British name for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something characteristic is typical of a person or thing: synonyms.

clue.text: Part sympathetic part pretentious

indicators.note: part means a portion, so the letters are a section of the two words

explanation.surface: A person who is partly kind and partly showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Artsy describes affected interest in the arts, a pretentious arty pose.

clue.text: Wander right off — or not

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to wander is to stray

explanation.surface: A choice: roam the right path away, or don't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or not' defines by reference: not wandering means remaining where you are.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain in place is the opposite of roaming, which the clue's 'or not' points to.

clue.text: Allow Bernstein to lie regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Permitting the composer Leonard Bernstein to tell an untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone to something is to give them the right to it, to allow it.

clue.text: Gossip about City's coach

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chat goes round the city

parts.note: to gossip is to chat
Rio, short for Rio de Janeiro

explanation.surface: Talk about a football club's manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's coach' suggests a football manager; the coach is a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn carriage, and coach is another name for one.

clue.text: Island heaven, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken, so the spelling may change

parts.note: the heavens are the sky

explanation.surface: People say a certain island is paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This one is a large island of the Inner Hebrides, so the definition names its kind.

clue.text: Live for nothing in ostentatious place at the top

indicators.note: for means instead of, so one piece replaces the other

parts.note: poncy is British slang for showy or affected
nothing is zero, the letter O
to live somewhere is to reside

explanation.surface: Living for free in a flashy house at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts RESIDE in place of the O of PONCY, a British slang word for pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A presidency is the office at the head of an organisation or state, the top position.
